title: Shakira’s Back with a World Cup Song—and This Time, She Brought a Friend!
summary:
Do you remember dancing to “Waka Waka” during the World Cup? Shakira’s back with a brand-new song for this year’s tournament, and it’s super catchy! It’s called “Dai Dai,” which means “come on, come on” in Italian. She teamed up with Burna Boy, a Nigerian singer who’s a huge star in Africa and around the world.

The song is a mix of Latin pop and Afrobeats—a style from West Africa that makes you want to move. The lyrics name-check famous soccer players like Pelé, Maradona, and Cristiano Ronaldo, plus countries playing in the World Cup like Brazil, England, and the U.S. It’s like a musical pep rally!

But “Dai Dai” isn’t just for fun. Every time someone streams it, money goes to a fund that helps kids get an education and play soccer. FIFA, the group that runs the World Cup, hopes to raise $100 million by the end of the tournament. That’s enough to build a lot of schools and soccer fields!

Shakira knows how to make World Cup hits. Her song “Waka Waka” from 2010 is the most-streamed World Cup song ever on Spotify—over a billion listens! She also performed at the 2006 and 2014 World Cups. This year, she’ll sing at the very first halftime show during the final match in New Jersey, along with Madonna and BTS.

Music has been part of the World Cup since 1930. Back then, it was local bands. Now, FIFA picks global stars to get everyone excited. Ricky Martin’s “The Cup of Life” in 1998 was a game-changer—it made him a superstar. Maybe “Dai Dai” will do the same for Burna Boy!
why_it_matters: It shows how your favorite songs can actually help other kids get an education and play the sports they love, connecting music, soccer, and making a difference.

background_read: FIFA (the International Federation of Association Football) has been organizing the World Cup, a global soccer tournament, every four years since 1930.
Official songs have fired up fans since the 1960s, and Shakira's 'Waka Waka' became a worldwide anthem during the 2010 World Cup in South Africa.
Today, World Cup songs often blend different music styles, like Latin pop and Afrobeats, to represent fans from many continents.
Article_Structure: WHO: Shakira and Burna Boy, along with name-checked soccer stars like Pelé and Cristiano Ronaldo.
WHAT: The release of 'Dai Dai,' a high-energy World Cup song that mixes Latin and Afrobeats sounds and raises money for children.
WHERE: The song will be performed at the final match in New Jersey, United States.
WHY: To rally fans around the tournament, celebrate soccer legends, and fund education and sports for kids worldwide.
